defects.claim: Deleting a region omits diagram descendants nested behind a plain group, since the reporting path recurses only through region children, so nested shapes and their attached connectors go unreported
A queued batched edit is delivered to the latest onEdit callback rather than the one current when the edit was reported, misapplying it to a replaced document or dropping it
A data node's own colors.header / colors.headerText are missing from ownStyle, so a theme change overwrites them
defects.scenario: `DataNode { rows: [{ kind: 'header', text: 'T' }, …], colors: { header: '#f00' } }` → `diagramScene` draws the band red (`withColors` applies `header`, `headerFillOf` writes `headerFill`), but `ownNodeStyle` lists only `fill`/`stroke`/`text`. A theme change then repaints the band from the theme (`themeWrites.paintBand` recolors to `look.style.header`, or drops `headerFill` when the theme names no header), losing the author's color. `DataNode.colors` documents "Each one set is listed in the trait's `ownStyle`, so a theme change leaves it." Same for `headerText`, which colors the header row's text.

defects.claim: relayoutBodies re-measures a row with no row node using the default style, so editing any other row changes that row's height
defects.scenario: a body built with `buildBody` whose `row` callback returns `null` for one styled label row (say `style: { fontSize: 20 }`, recorded height 24) carries a `body` record. Editing another row's text calls `relayoutBodies`; the declined row has no child in `rowNodes`, so it is rebuilt as `{ kind: 'label', text: '', style: rowStyle(undefined) }` and measured at the fallback line height. `heights` differs from `layout.heights`, the trait is rewritten, and every row below shifts up although nothing about that row changed. It should keep the recorded height for a row it cannot read back (as `recordedRows` does with a slot).
defects.cause: missing row node read as empty default-styled text

defects.claim: A connect can glue to a body whose every port showsPort hides, so the edge routes to a hidden port
defects.scenario: `showsPort: (p) => p.type === 'data'` on a node whose ports are all untyped, `bodies: true`. `portTarget` rejects every port, but `landing` accepts the body because `portsOf(...)` (unfiltered) is non-empty, and `portFor` resolves the body end with `resolveEnd` over all ports. The edge lands on and is drawn to a port the option documents as "never a target". `landing` and `portFor` should filter by `showsPort` the way `portTarget` does.
defects.cause: showsPort applied to port landings only, not body landings

defects.claim: A pool with no box nested in a boxed container gets no lane boxes, so its lanes vanish and its members have no seat
defects.scenario: `containers: [{ id: 'C', role: 'container', box: {...}, members: ['P'] }, { id: 'P', role: 'pool', lanes: [{ id: 'L', members: ['n'] }] }]`. P is hidden inside C, so layout never places it, and it has no `box`: `box === null` sends it down the "empty" branch (seated as `EMPTY_CONTAINER`, `continue`), skipping the pool branch that stacks its lanes. L never gets an entry in `out`. Node n (hidden, no `at`) is seated in L via `seatOf`, and `seedRows(..., bodyBox(out.get(L)!, ...))` gets `undefined` as the box: it throws or yields NaN rows. With `at` on n, `containerSpecs` still drops L (no box), leaving n's parent missing. The pool should be seeded at its default size (`DEFAULT_POOL_ACROSS` × lane sizes, as `startBox` gives a root pool) and its lanes stacked inside it.
defects.cause: nested unboxed pool treated as an empty container

defects.claim: A bounded view's limits come from the specs' poses rather than where a live layout moved the nodes
defects.scenario: `bounded` together with `ref.layout('force')`. The live layout moves nodes in the scene, but `diagramViewBounds(specs, ...)` reads only the given specs, and it recomputes only when they change. A node the run moves outside the specs' union can't be panned to. After the run settles, `fitting.settle()` fits `current()`, but `fitDiagram` clamps that fit to the same stale `bounds`, so the settle fit can't frame the moved nodes either.
defects.cause: bounds derived from specs, not the scene

defects.claim: Layered and tree layouts reserve no room for a cluster's minWidth when ranks run along x, so a titled cluster's box overlaps the next rank
defects.scenario: `diagramScene` gives a labeled cluster `minWidth = title + 2·pad` (dataClusters.ts `clusterMinWidth`), and `boxAround` widens its box evenly along x to that width. With a vertical layout, `packClusters`' `widen` reserves the room across. With `layoutOptions.direction` left-to-right (rank axis x), `widen` does nothing (`axes.cross === 0` is false) and `rankGaps` adds only insets. A one-rank cluster titled wider than its member therefore gets a box that grows into the gaps on either side and overlaps nodes, or other cluster boxes, in the neighboring ranks. `chain` handles the same case in `bandGaps` → `widenForMinWidth` (chainClusters.ts:197), so the two layouts answer one question two different ways. The rank gaps should widen as chain's do.
defects.cause: minWidth reserved only across ranks, not along them

defects.claim: DiagramViewApi.fit() and a settled layout fit against a 0 × 0 box while a filling view is still unmeasured
defects.scenario: A `DiagramView` with no `width`/`height` is 0 × 0 until `onResize` measures it. A host that calls `ref.current.fit()` in its mount effect, or a `layout()` that settles first, reaches `fitDiagram` with size 0 × 0. `fitViewToBounds` warns ("viewport has zero or negative area") and returns the identity view passed in, and `fitNow` sets that view on the canvas. The refit effect guards `unsized`; `settle` and `fitNow` do not. Both should no-op, or defer, until the box is measured.

defects.claim: useDiagramFit's defaultView memo omits fit.bounds from its deps, so the opening fit stays clamped to stale bounds
defects.scenario: `fitDiagram` clamps the fit to `fit.bounds` so that the view the canvas holds is the fit itself, and a later fit still sees the view as untouched. The memo's deps list `minScale`, `maxScale`, `anchor` and `padding` but not `bounds`. When `bounded` turns on after mount, or the bounded specs change and `viewBounds` changes, `defaultView` keeps its old clamp, or none. The canvas then clamps the view against the new `viewBounds` itself, `canvas.getView()` stops matching `fitted.current`, and the target effect's `sameView` check reads every later refit as a user pan and drops it.

defects.claim: clusterBoxes wraps a cluster's box around its members' bare boxes, while CLUSTER_DERIVE_POSE grows each member by its margin, so the box and the members' margins disagree
defects.scenario: a clustered node with `portLabels` gets a `margin` on its trait (bodyTrait → marginOf). `clusterBoxes` takes the union of `placedAt.get(m)` with no margin. `clusterDerivePose` (clusterBox.ts:91) and `placeContainers`' fitted-container footprint (dataContainerPlace.ts:111) both apply `grownBy(…, margin)`. So the cluster spec's pose, which `scenePageSplits` and `fitDiagram`/`diagramViewBounds` read from specs, is smaller than the box the scene derives and draws. The port labels fall outside the box as the specs report it. Two answers to one box.

defects.claim: A pool box too small for its unsized lanes lets the lanes stack past the box
defects.scenario: a pool with `box.height: 100` and three lanes that give no `size`. `share` = 33.3 and each lane is clamped up to `MIN_LANE_SIZE` (40). The last-lane correction is clamped to 40 again, so the lanes total 120. `stackedLanes` (dataContainerPlace.ts:83) places them from the box's top, and the third lane runs 20 units below the pool. The pool box is never grown to fit. Given sizes over `along` also get the last lane silently cut down (lanes of 150 and 150 in a box of 200 come out 150 and 50).
defects.cause: min clamp applied after the share, never reconciled with the box

defects.claim: buildBody gives leaves world poses but also sets parent, so spreading them into a rigid scene offsets every row twice
defects.scenario: `buildBody` is public (index.ts:30, layout.entry.ts:37), and its doc says a consumer "can still spread one". With `id` set, each leaf gets `parent: opts.id` and a pose laid out at the body's world `x, y` (`layoutBody(spec, pose)`). Under the scene's default `RIGID_POSE_COMPOSITION`, a child pose is stored in its parent's frame, so a body at (200, 100) draws its rows at about (400, 200). Both internal callers know to run `localizeWorldPoses` first (fromData.ts:147, stencil.ts:120), but nothing in `buildBody`'s docs says the poses are world. Its sibling `relayoutBodies` expects rows in the body's frame.
defects.cause: undocumented frame contract on public output

defects.claim: startFrom: 'body' starts a connect from a body with no ports, which landing refuses as a target
defects.scenario: connector tool (`startFrom: 'body'`, `bodies: true`) pressed on a participant whose `portsOf` is empty (e.g. `ports: []`). `startEnd` takes `bodyAt(...)` with no port check, so the drag starts; the preview's `portFor(fixed, …)` resolves no port and draws nothing, yet a release on a valid target commits an edge glued to a body with nothing to route to. `connectTargets.landing` rejects exactly this case for the other end ("A body with no ports is nothing, since an edge glued to it has nothing to route to"), so the two ends answer the same question differently.
defects.cause: port-less body check only on the landing side

defects.claim: relayoutBodies measures a field row differently from the build, dropping its room
defects.scenario: a body built with `{ kind: 'field', label: 'Name', value: 'x', room: 'XXXXXXXXXXXX' }`: `measureRow` floors its width at label + 2·gap + max(value, room). After any text edit `relayoutBodies` rebuilds every non-header row as `{ kind: 'label', text: 'Name: x' }`, measuring the concatenated string instead — no `room`, ": " in place of the 8-unit gap. The floor a field puts under the body is thus answered two ways (build vs. relayout); a value typed in past the old box grows the body by the label-row width, not the field width the build used, and `room`'s promise ("a value written in later fits the box it already has") is not what relayout checks against.
defects.cause: field rows not recorded as fields in `BodyLayout`

defects.claim: DiagramViewApi.worldAt returns client coordinates as world coordinates when the canvas is not mounted
defects.scenario: a host calls `ref.current.worldAt(e.clientX, e.clientY)` for a drop while the canvas ref is still null (before mount, or after it unmounts). It gets `{ x: clientX, y: clientY }` back as a world point and inserts the item at a meaningless spot. Its siblings `visible` and `rectOf` return `null` in the same state, so the caller has no way to tell this answer is wrong.

defects.claim: A container stencil's ghost is drawn dashed, but the container it inserts is never dashed
defects.scenario: drag a container or pool stencil from a palette with `style` carrying `dash: [4, 4]` → the ghost is stroked with `strokeDasharray="4 4"`, but a placed region is outlined through `outlineOf(style, 'region')` (dataTypes.ts), which drops `dash` for a region, so the ghost shows an outline the drop will not produce. The ghost should read the dash the same way (`outlineOf(own, 'region')` for a `ContainerStencil`, `'body'` for a shape).
defects.cause: ghost reads dash directly instead of through outlineOf

defects.claim: A queued batched edit still calls onEdit after the view has unmounted, because the pending batch is not canceled on unmount
defects.scenario: a gesture or layout run reports `onMove` and then the view unmounts in the same task. For example, the host swaps the diagram out in response to the same `onMove`. The queued microtask still calls `latest.current.onEdit` with that batch, after teardown, so the host can write an edit into data for a view that no longer exists. Nothing cancels the pending batch on unmount or when `batching` turns off.
